title: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol)
summary: IMAP is a protocol for accessing email on a server. Unlike POP3, IMAP keeps messages on the server and supports folders, search, and partial fetch. Commands: LOGIN, SELECT, EXAMINE, CREATE, DELETE, RENAME, SUBSCRIBE, LIST, LSUB, STATUS, APPEND, CHECK, CLOSE, EXPUNGE, SEARCH, FETCH, STORE, COPY, UID, IDLE, NAMESPACE, CAPABILITY, LOGOUT. Responses: OK, NO, BAD, PREAUTH, BYE.

ext.summary: IMAP is a protocol for accessing email on a server. Unlike POP3, IMAP keeps messages on the server and supports folders, search, and partial fetch. Commands: LOGIN, SELECT, EXAMINE, CREATE, DELETE, RENAME, SUBSCRIBE, LIST, LSUB, STATUS, APPEND, CHECK, CLOSE, EXPUNGE, SEARCH, FETCH, STORE, COPY, UID, IDLE, NAMESPACE, CAPABILITY, LOGOUT. Responses: OK, NO, BAD, PREAUTH, BYE.

structure.meaning: Select a mailbox: SELECT INBOX. Returns mailbox status (exists, recent, unseen, uidnext, uidvalidity).
Fetch message data: FETCH 1:10 (FLAGS BODY[HEADER]). Returns message content.
Search messages: SEARCH UNSEEN, SEARCH FROM sender, SEARCH SINCE date, SEARCH TEXT keyword.
Wait for new messages. Server pushes notifications. Client sends DONE to exit.
UID-based variants: UID FETCH, UID SEARCH, UID STORE, UID COPY, UID MOVE.
List server capabilities: IMAP4rev2, STARTTLS, AUTH=PLAIN, IDLE, MOVE, etc.

notes: IMAP keeps messages on the server (unlike POP3 which downloads and deletes).
IMAP supports multiple mailboxes (folders) and hierarchical folder structure.
IDLE command enables push notifications for new mail.
IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051) is the latest version, obsoleting IMAP4rev1.
